e.etymology: An English surname meaning son of Judd, where Judd was a medieval short form of Jordan. American families used it as a first name in the 1800s, often in honor of the Baptist missionary Adoniram Judson.
The French form of Violet, from violette, the diminutive of Old French viole, from Latin viola, the violet flower.
The Greek and Latin form of Jeremiah, from Hebrew Yirmeyahu, the Lord exalts. It is the form used in Spanish, Portuguese and German, and for the prophet in the King James New Testament.
An English surname from a place name, Old English for white island. As a girls' name it took off in the 1980s with the fame of singer Whitney Houston.

assoc.t: Whitney Houston, the pop and R&B singer
Mount Whitney, tallest peak in the lower 48 states
the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York

e.etymology: From the Kenai Peninsula and Kenai River in Alaska, named for the Kenaitze, the Dena'ina people of the region. The hero of Disney's 2003 film Brother Bear is also called Kenai.

assoc.t: Kenai Peninsula and Kenai River in Alaska
Kenai, the hero of Disney's Brother Bear

e.meaning: God is gracious (John) or God has given (Jonathan)
e.etymology: A spelling of John, from Hebrew Yochanan, God is gracious, and the usual short form of Jonathan, God has given. In Scandinavia Jon is the old native form of John, from Old Norse.
namesakes: Jon Stewart (host of The Daily Show)
Jon Snow (hero of Game of Thrones)

e.etymology: A modern American coinage, most likely a blend of Aubrey and Gabriella.
A Spanish-language elaboration of Julia with the -issa ending of Melissa and Clarissa. The Mexican actress and singer Julissa, born Julia Isabel, made it known from the 1960s.
A name with unrelated sources: Turkish kaya means rock, and Kaya is also a Japanese name. In the US it rose after American Girl introduced Kaya, a Nez Perce character, in 2002.
namesakes: Kaya Scodelario (actress in The Maze Runner films)

assoc.t: Kaya, the Nez Perce American Girl doll
Kaya, 1978 Bob Marley album; slang for marijuana

e.etymology: From French Eugene, Latin Eugenius, Greek Eugenios: eu, well, and the root for born. Several early saints and four popes bore the name, and it was in the US top 30 in the 1920s.
namesakes: Eugene Fitzherbert (Flynn Rider in Disney's Tangled)

assoc.t: Eugene, Oregon

e.etymology: A short form of Evan, Ivan, Vance or Donovan, and the Dutch surname particle meaning of or from. Van is also a Vietnamese name, from words for literature (for men) and cloud (for women).
namesakes: Van Morrison (singer-songwriter of Brown Eyed Girl)

assoc.t: van, the boxy vehicle
Vans, skate shoe and apparel brand

e.note: Also the everyday word for a vehicle, so expect the occasional joke.

e.etymology: As a first name, a respelling of Ivy, the plant name, in the form of the English surname Ivey.
A modern name with no single established source; it is read as a spelling of Rhea, Raya or the Indian name Riya.
From Old Norse Leifr, heir or descendant. Its best-known bearer is Leif Erikson, the Norse explorer who reached North America around the year 1000.
namesakes: Leif Erikson (Norse explorer who reached North America)
e.note: Scandinavians say LAYF; many Americans say LEEF, like leaf, so expect to correct people either way.

assoc.t: Leif Erikson, Norse explorer who reached North America

e.etymology: The Spanish and Portuguese form of Rachel, from Hebrew rachel, ewe. In Genesis Rachel is the beloved wife of Jacob and mother of Joseph and Benjamin.

assoc.t: Raquel Welch, 1960s film star

e.etymology: An English surname read as son of Wes, with Wes a short form of Wesley. As a first name it is recent and American, and best known from the gunmaker Smith & Wesson.

assoc.t: Smith & Wesson, the firearms maker
Wesson cooking oil

e.note: Most people will connect it with Smith & Wesson firearms, and some with Wesson cooking oil.

e.etymology: A modern American elaboration of Ava with the -yah ending of names such as Aaliyah and Amaya.

e.meaning: a king's daughter; a royal title
e.etymology: The English title used as a given name. The word comes through French from Latin princeps, first or chief.

assoc.t: princess, the royal title; Disney princesses
princess, a teasing word for a pampered person

e.note: Doubles as a title and as a teasing word for someone seen as spoiled.

e.etymology: A name used mainly in Mexican and Mexican American families. It is usually taken as a form of Areli, a minor Biblical name from Genesis, though the link is not certain.
A form of French Celine, usually traced to Latin Caelina, from caelum, sky or heaven. Celine has also served as a short form of Marceline, and Celina is sometimes used as a spelling of Selina.

From Hebrew Zekharyah, the Lord has remembered. The Bible has many Zechariahs, among them an Old Testament prophet and the father of John the Baptist. Zachary and Zachariah are forms of the same name.
A modern American name that extends Kai with the -sen ending of Jensen, in the same family as Kaison and Kayson. Many people know the word from the Japanese anime Jujutsu Kaisen.

assoc.t: Jujutsu Kaisen, a hit Japanese manga and anime

e.meaning: mighty in battle, by way of Matilda
e.etymology: A pet form of Matilda, from the Germanic words for might and battle. Tilly and Tillie were used on their own in the 1800s and have come back with Millie and Elsie.

assoc.t: Tillys, teen clothing and skate shoe chain

e.etymology: A K spelling of Colson, an English surname meaning son of Cole, where Cole was a medieval short form of Nicholas.
A minor Old Testament name: Jasiel, also written Jaasiel, is one of King David's warriors in 1 Chronicles. It is from Hebrew for God makes, and is used today mostly in Spanish-speaking families.
A German and Scandinavian short form of Elisabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, my God is an oath. English speakers met it through the heroine of Wagner's opera Lohengrin and, since 2013, Disney's Frozen.
namesakes: Elsa (the snow queen of Disney's Frozen)

assoc.t: Disney's Frozen queen
Elsa the lioness of Born Free

e.note: Since 2013 most people think of Frozen first; expect Let It Go references.

e.meaning: son of Maud, or son of Matthew
e.etymology: A modern spelling of Madison, an English surname meaning son of Maud or son of Matthew. Madison became a girls' name after the 1984 film Splash.
A spelling of Layla or Leila, from Arabic layla, night. The name is famous from the old Arabic and Persian love story of Layla and Majnun.

assoc.t: Layla, Eric Clapton's 1970 rock classic

e.etymology: A modern American blend of Wren, the small songbird, and the -leigh spelling of the -ley ending found in Paisley and Everleigh.

A surname-style name of uncertain source, grouped with Irish names such as Kellan and Kelly; there is also a German surname Kellen. NFL tight end Kellen Winslow brought it to American attention around 1980.
namesakes: Kellen Winslow (Hall of Fame NFL tight end)
Kellen Moore (NFL quarterback turned head coach)

e.etymology: In the US a modern name in the style of Aria and Amaya. Araya is also a Spanish surname of Basque origin and a Thai given name.
